--- stdout
[1/10] Checking this machine
[2/10] Settings

SuckerPot participant mode (experimental preview)

This machine will run honeypot sensors and send what they see to a hub run by the
SuckerPot maintainers. What is sent, once a day and a few hours late:
  - source addresses seen by your sensors, with the services they used, what they did and
    rounded counts;
  - download links attackers tried, as hashes; the clear link goes to the hub only when two or
    more sensors saw the same link, so a verifier can check it;
  - malware hashes and command-and-control addresses (only with a VPN and the collector);
  - takedown checks for addresses the network reported.
Never sent: passwords, commands, your ports, your own address or names in any payload.

What you get back today: nothing yet. The shared feed is an experimental preview and stays
empty until enough independent nodes exist. Its thresholds and protocol may change.

The hub is reached through a Cloudflare tunnel, so Cloudflare and the hub both see the
address the request comes from.
Without a VPN that address is this machine's own public address, so it is not hidden.
Add a VPN at any time: ./scripts/participant.sh vpn <file.conf>
Updates: checked every 6 h, a signed release installs once 48 h old (off: --no-auto-update). The
update checks contact GitHub, ghcr.io and Sigstore from this machine's own address, even
with a VPN. Without a VPN, the hub name is also looked up through your normal DNS resolver.
Leave at any time: ./scripts/participant.sh leave

Pseudonym: <pseudonym>   (change: --pseudonym NAME, none: --no-pseudonym)

--yes was given: this counts as your agreement to join as described above.

SuckerPot is running in participant mode (v0.8.0).
  Pseudonym: <pseudonym>   Hub: suckerpot-hub.selfhostr.io   Path: direct (no VPN)

Open these ports on your router or firewall, all to this machine:
  Router port   ->  This machine  Protocol   Sensor
  22            ->  22            TCP        ssh
  80            ->  80            TCP        web
  443           ->  443           TCP        web
Never forward the admin SSH port of this machine.
Use port forwards, not your router's DMZ. A DMZ puts every service of this machine on the
internet, the real sshd included. It is acceptable only if this machine runs nothing else
and its admin SSH port is not 22. The host firewall does not filter internet traffic to this
machine's own services: under a DMZ the admin SSH faces the internet, so allow key-only SSH
and add a rule on the router or on this machine for the admin port.

Host firewall
  Admin SSH port used: 22 (default). If that is wrong, set ADMIN_SSH_PORT in .env and run again.
  The host firewall needs sudo, which asks for a password here. To install it now, run:
    ./scripts/participant.sh firewall

Check it any time:      ./scripts/status.sh

The network counts your sensor after a short probation period set by the hub. The date shows in ./scripts/status.sh.
Take a snapshot of this machine now if you can.
